A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RouterArena and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–D. All 16 pages were compared; the appendices are identical in text and rendered appearance.

before.justification: v1 reports original router evaluations in Section 6, including accuracy–cost comparisons, routing optimality, robustness, latency, and leaderboard rankings.

after.justification: v2 retains these original evaluations, including Table 2 and Figures 5–8, with the supplementary leaderboard visualization in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The dataset construction procedure, Arena scoring method, and automated evaluation workflow are unchanged. Figure 4 depicts the same procedure despite its changed rendering.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 8,400-query dataset drawn from 23 sources, covering nine domains, 44 categories, and three difficulty levels. The evaluated input-perturbation scenario is also unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership within Table 2 and Figures 5–8 is unchanged. Both retain the same academic routers and commercial comparisons involving Azure-Router, NotDiamond, and GPT-5.

E3.justification: Sections 4–6 retain the same metrics, cost normalization, default Arena weight, training arrangements, budget-based masking, perturbation procedure, and latency measurement setting. Appendix A's model pools are unchanged.

E4.justification: The normalized deferral analysis, actual-versus-optimal routing comparison, and noisy-input robustness analysis are retained without revision. No ablations, robustness tests, or supplementary analyses are added or removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. There is no change in statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Numerical results, rankings, and reported trends match. For example, Figure 1 retains Arena scores of 67.3 for MIRT-BERT and 66.4 for Azure-Router; Table 2 and the result plots also retain their values.

T1.justification: The metric definitions and Section 5.1's logarithmic cost normalization and weighted harmonic Arena score are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: Both versions make the same core contributions: a comprehensive router comparison platform, a principled dataset, multiple evaluation metrics, and automated evaluation. The scientific conclusions about accuracy–cost trade-offs and inefficient routing remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The interpretations of commercial versus academic routers, inefficient use of expensive models, robustness, and latency are unchanged. The qualification that opaque commercial routers prevent measurement of certain metrics is also retained.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces the promise to open the platform with a GitHub repository location, RouteWorks/RouterArena, for evaluating new routers. This adds concrete access information; implementation settings, hardware information, model pools, and appendix prompts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference list, benchmark comparison in Table 1, and research positioning in Sections 2 and 7 are unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract's closing sentence is revised to identify the framework repository. Apart from version/date text and reflow, the wording, section organization, and appendix structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 4 changes from a vector/text diagram to a raster image of the same workflow, with slightly softer lettering. Minor text and figure-position reflow occurs in the main text; other display content and the appendix layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The abstract now provides a concrete framework repository location instead of only promising a future release, modestly improving access information. Scientific evidence and arguments are unchanged. Figure 4's rasterization slightly reduces sharpness, and Section 5.2 retains future-release wording, so the overall benefit is limited.
